s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of dyspnea, palpitations, and lightheadedness with ventricular tachycardia
salient_findings: Abrupt onset of dyspnea, palpitations, and lightheadedness
Markedly dilated right ventricle with severely reduced systolic function
key_facts: 66-year-old white man
Presented to the Emergency Department with abrupt onset of symptoms
Found to be in monomorphic ventricular tachycardia
Electrically cardioverted into normal sinus rhythm
Medical history includes cerebrovascular accident, Factor V Leiden and prothrombin gene mutations, hypertension, incidentally noted pulmonary nodules, and chronic kidney disease
Taking losartan and warfarin
No family history of sudden cardiac death
Initial laboratory studies were within normal limits
Coronary angiography ruled out ischemia
Electrocardiogram showed normal sinus rhythm without ischemic changes, but an epsilon wave in V1, a QRS duration of 140 ms, and T-wave inversions in leads V1–V5
Transthoracic echocardiography revealed preserved left ventricular function and no valvular disease, but a markedly dilated right ventricle with severely reduced systolic function

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Epsilon wave in V1, T-wave inversions in V1-V3, and severely reduced right ventricular systolic function

shortlist.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Pulmonary nodules and right ventricular dysfunction

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia

shortlist.label: Right ventricular outflow tract tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia and right ventricular dilation

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Ventricular tachycardia without clear ischemic or structural cause

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with monomorphic ventricular tachycardia, epsilon wave in V1, QRS duration of 140 ms, T-wave inversions in leads V1–V5, and markedly dilated right ventricle with severely reduced systolic function on echocardiography are consistent with arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia.

rejected.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Although it remains in the differential diagnosis due to pulmonary nodules, the specific electrocardiogram and echocardiography findings point more towards arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: This is essentially synonymous with arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia, but the provided information best supports the chosen champion without needing to differentiate between these closely related conditions.

rejected.label: Right ventricular outflow tract tachycardia
rejected.why: The patient's presentation with ventricular tachycardia and the findings on echocardiography do not specifically support this diagnosis as much as they support arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia.

rejected.label: Idiopathic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: The presence of structural heart disease, as indicated by the dilated right ventricle and reduced systolic function, contradicts the 'idiopathic' classification.
